name: Sensitive Skin
description: Sensitive skin is a common condition characterized by irritation, itching, redness, and discomfort that can be triggered by various factors. This type of skin reacts more strongly than normal to external irritants or allergens.
causes: Chemical ingredients in cosmetics and detergents
symptoms: Redness and flushing of the skin
Sensitivity to temperature changes (hot or cold)
risk_factors: History of allergic reactions or asthma
recommended_ingredients: Niacinamide (vitamin B3) to reduce redness and inflammation
Squalane for its non-comedogenic properties and moisturizing benefits
Green tea extract for anti-inflammatory effects
ingredients_to_avoid: Sulfates, as they can be harsh on the skin
Parabens and other preservatives that might cause irritation
Alcohol, which can strip the skin of its natural oils
recommended_product_categories: Sunscreen with physical or chemical filters

daily_routine.purpose: Remove dirt and impurities without stripping the skin of its natural oils.
Restore the skin's pH balance and prepare it for further products.
Lock in moisture and provide necessary hydration to maintain skin barrier integrity.

professional_treatments: Intense Pulsed Light (IPL) for hyperpigmentation and redness
natural_remedies: Applying aloe vera gel to soothe irritated skin
Using oatmeal baths or face masks for calming effects
lifestyle_tips: Wear protective clothing when outdoors in harsh weather conditions.
Conduct patch tests on new skincare items before full application.
common_myths: Sensitive skin can be completely cured by stopping use of irritating products.
All sensitive skin types require the same type of treatment or product line.
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist despite avoiding known triggers, or if there is a sudden onset of severe irritation and swelling.
prevention: Identify and avoid personal trigger factors
Use gentle skincare products free from harsh chemicals

severity_levels.mild: Mild cases may show symptoms such as occasional redness, itching, or tightness after using certain products.
severity_levels.moderate: Moderate cases might experience more frequent and intense reactions to common irritants. Symptoms could persist for several days following exposure to triggers.
severity_levels.severe: Severe cases involve persistent skin issues that affect daily activities and quality of life. There may be significant discomfort, visible signs of inflammation, and increased risk of secondary infections.

expert_tips: Always patch test new products before full application
Consult a dermatologist regularly to tailor treatment plans according to individual needs
